title: A greyscale mask carrying `tRNS`
why: The mask is greyscale with **no alpha**, and `tRNS` is how a greyscale PNG carries alpha anyway — so this is the one place the chunk allowlist and the mask's own encoding rule disagree, since `tRNS` is legitimately permitted on the accepted candidate. Left admitted, the decode gives a matching sample alpha `0` while the coverage scan reads only the grey channel: a transparent white pixel would suppress a comparison here and refuse the mask on a consumer enforcing the no-alpha rule as written. Refused in the same `IHDR` preflight that already decides the encoding.
